key_insight: A single LLM can act as both an agent and its own next-tool-call speculator, reducing tool latency by predicting and pre-executing the agent’s next action from partial trajectories.
engineering_relevance: This simplifies deployment by reusing one model and one prefix KV cache, making tool-augmented systems faster without adding a separate draft/speculator model.
method: Train a self-speculating agent in two modes: agent mode for task solving and speculator mode for predicting the next tool call.
Use joint agent-speculator reinforcement learning to derive speculation targets from the agent’s own rollouts.
Alternate updates between agent and speculator behavior so speculation aligns with the deployed agent.
evidence_signal: On agentic search QA and conversational tool-use tasks, average next-tool-call Hit@1 improved from 44.1 to 61.2 for Qwen3-4B and from 48.9 to 66.3 for Qwen3.5-4B, while maintaining task success.
watch_item: The approach depends on the model’s ability to preserve agent performance while learning speculation, so RL stability and mismatch between predicted and actual tool calls remain practical concerns.
paper_title: Speculate While You Reason: Teaching Agents to Predict Their Next Tool Call via Joint Agent-Speculator RL
